facts.raw_span: A 34-year old African American woman
history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
painless, left upper eyelid mass
previously been excised on 3 separate occasions
painless proptosis
left-sided facial numbness seventeen months later
Histopathology: Revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
Axial T1-weighted fat-saturated postgadolinium MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment

Axial T1-weighted postgadolinium MRI shows tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery with extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus and with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Next-generation sequencing of the tumor demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the partner and localizer of BRCA2 (PALB2)

concepts.why: Histopathology revealed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells demonstrating increased mitotic activity, and immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68.

Histopathology showed a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, and immunohistochemistry was positive for CD68, which are features consistent with Rosai-Dorfman Disease.

The presence of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells with increased mitotic activity, and positive immunohistochemistry for CD68, could be consistent with Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
The aggressive clinical course, histopathological features, and genetic findings, including a splicing variant in the PALB2 gene, could suggest Histiocytic Sarcoma.
The histopathological features, including a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, could be consistent with Dendritic Cell Sarcoma.
The presence of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, and positive immunohistochemistry for CD68, could suggest Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma.

The histopathological features, including a multinodular proliferation of osteoclastlike multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, could be consistent with Interdigitating Dendritic Cell Sarcoma.
The patient has a history of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma, which could be relevant to the current presentation.
The patient's history of Hodgkin lymphoma and the aggressive nature of the current tumor could suggest a secondary tumor.

rationales.F12: The presence of a PALB2 splicing variant suggests a possible link to PALB2-related tumors.
